content.body:
The next evolutionary step from the A15 Crusader II was meant to be the Cavalier. The failure of that program left the British military searching for some way to get 6 pdr guns in the field to cope with the heavier German tanks that were showing up more frequently in North Africa. Taking the quickest solution, they gave the Crusader chassis another upgrade and stuffed a 6 pdr gun into the turret. As an expedient, the Crusader III was quite successful though woefully thin by comparison to the German armor it faced.
Functionally almost identical to the previous Crusader II, the Crusader III is a better tank with a gun capable of killing most German AFV's. The green color and main armament make it excellent for ambush, although the characteristically weak British optics somewhat negate the range advantages of the QF 6 pdr gun. It remains very lightly armored, particularly in the later-war context. Drive it like an armored car. Pay close attention to your situation and don't stand and fight anything without moving to your advantage. Don't be afraid to stop and look around, as long as you’re in cover; the green coloring will hide you from cursory examination.
As with the Crusader II, you need to fear air attack because your top armor can be penetrated by fighter machineguns. You can lure enemy panzers closer to see if you have actually been completely destroyed in the event that you are disabled but not on fire, the color of your camouflage sometimes makes it hard to pick you out at range.
Control Variations:
The driver spawns in with view slit armor in place but can zoom when the view slit is open (numpad . or Del key). The O key opens a bigger view window, which can also be magnified. The gunner has no view slit, nor does his gun sight view display the range setting of the gun. This can be seen by pressing the grave accent (`) key (often misidentified as the "tilde" (~) key), and changed with the Page Up and Page Down keys.
